title: Entity file
description: One file per category under data/entities/. Each file is a flat array of entities. NO PROSE LIVES HERE: descriptions, epithets and blurbs belong in src/i18n/locales/<locale>/entities.json, keyed by entity.<id>.*. The Old Norse name is the one exception — it is the historical name, identical in every locale, and is data.

id.description: Stable, lowercase, ASCII. Never localized, never renamed once merged — ids are the join key for locale files, URLs and every relation.

type.description: What kind of thing this is. Drives node shape in the renderer.

classes.description: Grouping for colour and filtering. An entity may hold several — Loki is both aesir and jotnar, and that tension is the point.

non.description: Normalized Old Norse name, or the Old Norse term for a form node. This is DATA, not a translation: it is identical in every locale. Diacritics must be correct — þ ð æ ø ǫ á é í ó ú ý.

anglicized.description: The conventional English-language spelling, or the English gloss for a form node.

aliases.description: Alternative names and edition spellings for the same referent. These are historical/source data, not translated prose.

attestations.description: Source COLLECTIONS in which this entity appears, by id from data/sources.json. Relations cite individual works and loci; entities record the coarser fact of where they turn up at all.

tags.description: Controlled vocabulary. Drives the tag index behind the 'related but not adjacent' suggestions, and the Ragnarök overlay's selection of combatants. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: free-text tags would make the suggestion feature meaningless within a hundred entities.
